title.label: Superb Markdown editor on all my devices

content.label: Very happy to have such a beautifully-crafted editor syncing seamlessly across all my devices. I use Markdown (with the Markdown compatibility option), and with its superb keyboard support it makes creating notes and writing on my iPad a real pleasure. Keep up the good work! For the future, I'd love to see custom date formats (e.g. 2018/09/23), and secure notes.
If you’re looking for an alternative to the iPhone notes app definitely choose Bear! It’s amazing and so easy to use and organise, I’m so glad I found it! Much love for the team behind Bear
It’s excellent for both note taking and file storage, if it had LaTeX support i wouldn’t need to use anything else

title.label: Decent App on Mac But Currently Crashes on iOS

content.label: Very pleased with the functionality on my Mac but cannot get the app to run on iOS 12. Multiple devices tried.

title.label: Best note taking app I’ve ever used

content.label:
I’ve used Bear for over a year now and it’s changed the way I work. 
I no longer worry about forgetting ideas or wondering where they’re stored if I did manage to note them down.
Bear is easy to use and it’s features make writing a joy to organise.
Not sure if it just me but cant open the app

So I recently deleted and unsubscribed from this gorgeous application. I transferred all of my notes to the Apple notes app. (Instantly regretting my decision) now about a week later I am in the process of re-downloading and resubscribing as I simply just can’t go back! Such an amazing application and I can’t help but recommend it to everyone!
This app made me move from Evernote which I was using for nearly 5 years! Very well design led and beautiful app

It’s very handy for quick notes, specially if you have multiple devices and you wanna sync them. I got the pro version because the syncing option is really handy. I like the way the notes can be easily formatted to suit your needs to make lists or just reminders.

title.label: The drawing is vague in the note

content.label:
It is clear on the note list page, it is fine when you click on the drawing to open the drawing page.
But if you view it in the note, it is vague, you can see the fuzzy edge on the drawings.

title.label: Amazing app love the to do checklist option

content.label:
It’s great for making to do lists and printing them. Wonderful for storing some quick stories and notes. 
The search is powerful but loses a star as the search does not search any of your archives.
Really simple and powerful

I think bear is one of the best apps I had for notes (and I had many). That's because it's all I ever wanted - sleek and aesthetic, simple and elegant design and look, easy to operate and has so many options that many apps don't offer (and we can't forget about the fonts!)
The app is cute in general, I love bear 😊🐻

title.label: Hassle free noting at its finest

content.label:
This app does absolutely everything you need! I had used a few others such as the default notes app and onenote but kept coming back here and now I don't think I'll ever leave  :)

It is super powerful yet so simple to use. It makes taking notes at work fun. I can embed images, draw key things and also add checklists etc for later. It syncs seamlessly between all my devices which is a key requirement and it fulfills that task perfectly. The ability to easily export notes out to PDF is super useful and means I don't have to carry around multiple notebooks anymore. Also it gets the job done, is not clunky and is stable too. Highly recommend!
Genuinely makes writing notes more enjoyable, organisation is much easier, and the it is just aesthetically effortlessly pleasing. Would love to see a voice recording feature in it as well.
Really excellent app. Love the layout and style. Really easy to use and has great organising functionality.

I used to really enjoy this app, but it’s lost two really important notes now and that’s two too many. Would rather go back to using Apple Notes which is at least reliable even if it doesn’t have as many bells and whistles

I really like and really wanted to use Bear, but the lack of the concept of Notebook and Shared Notebook (like there is in Ulysses) has forced me to move :( will be back as soon as they implement this (if it’s soon enough and will be easy to import my notes)
Love this app to bits.  Makes writing a real pleasure - even boring stuff like meeting notes etc.  Simple but very effective.  And fun - loving the Tagcons!! Well worth the subscription.

title.label: Finally an app to replace Evernote

content.label: At last I've found a suitable replacement for Evernote at a much more acceptable price point. Easy to export all my notes from Evernote too. I really like the interface and find the app very user friendly. Congrats to the Bear Dev team. Keep up the good work.

I trusted the Apple review of bear but it seems that the praise was aimed at the design and not the function of this app. DO download if you like beautiful note taking. DON’T download if you like spare time and flawless syncing. Don’t take my word for it - search for “sync problem” and “bear” to see what I mean. I have spent a day trying to fix this and no joy. Stick with Evernote is my advise.

title.label: Love the app, but not loving the sync.

content.label: I’ve been using Bear on my iPad to collect thoughts and observations during the day, and for that, it works well. However, I'm less than thrilled by the fact that syncing happens when I open Bear directly, but not when I'm sending links, text snippet to it from other apps. Since that is pretty much THE main reason for getting the Pro subscription, I've cancelled my trial and will pass my notes over to Ulysses at the end of each day.

There are a LOT of notes apps out there right now and I’ve tried most of them. 

This is now going to replace Mosaic as far as I’m concerned. The UX is stunning and the Mac app (which syncs perfectly and speedily) is the icing on the cake. 

Well done developers.

I love, love, love Bear. The Pro version gives access to beautiful themes and neat file import and export options. It's really affordable, too. 

I have absolutely no complaints. It is by miles the best note taking/editing app out there. Maybe consider making a pink/berry coloured theme one day?

title.label: Like a pair of comfy slippers

content.label: What you need, right there, when you need it. Gets out of its own way like no other app in its category. A joy to use. The end of years of searching. And at a good price. Well done Bear.

Bear is a delight to use, it makes you want to write, for me it's the best notes app. Tags have improved so much but I would still like folders as well as tags. And lastly it would be amazing if one could fold text in long notes, simply, collapse everything other than the part of the note you are working on.

title.label: Tried every notes app but sticking with Bear

content.label:
I’ve tried probably 15 different notes apps for my personal and business note taking needs. For me this is the best. A proper hierarchical but simple tag hierarchy is the killer feature for me. And a beautiful simple interface. 

My only additional feature requests would be:

1. Setting to disable touch drawing in sketches when using Apple Pencil
2. Infinite vertical scrolling on sketches so that I can create hand written lengthy notes in a meeting when I need to

Thanks and keep it coming team Bear.
Very good. I like this.
Best app I’ve ever found

After a year of using Bear I’ve cancelled my subscription.
If I’m taking notes in a business meeting the last thing I want are childish cartoons and cheesy out of date slogans like ‘Keep calm and write something’ appearing - it’s a bit like something designed by an old aunt.

Additionally, a simple note-taking app just isn’t worth a subscription, supporting this model means more and more developers will move to it.

I can’t understand why there is no option to export ePub. Ulysses does this so well. In bear the option is to export to pdf, docx, markdown, but no ePub! Such a shame.
I also need Dropbox sync. My subscription has gone to Ulysses for these simple reasons.

title.label: A bit too complicated for me

content.label: I’m sure Bear is a brilliant app but for me it’s a bit too complex. I’m used to a more straightforward way of keeping notes, I don’t want to keep trying to remember tags and various commands etc. I’ll stick with ‘Notes Plus’ and ‘Keep’ I also don’t like subscription apps and always avoid them. Having said that you should try Bear as it may well work for you.

Why use it when you have a OneNote is beyond me. Someone wrote that he needs to leave his chrome book and take iPad while on the road to use this app but... it’s great according to him haha. It’s crazy. Proper app needs to synchronise with all systems and doesn’t look so dull

title.label: Super Brilliant and Exciting. Versatile and Brave.

content.label:
So, before I wrote this I thought I’d have a look at the one star reviews because I wanted to see what it is that I am not seeing, where is the broken parts? It might be that BEAR have taken on board what people have said, because there is now a one off payment for the pro version so that’s some of these negatives already striked out. I find their Twitter team to be charming, responsive and super fun so the complaints about tech support are confusing to me. Other than that, people are marking this down for not being Apple Notes/Evernote/Day One [delete as applicable]. It’s not any of them. It doesn’t say it is. When you read the blurb, nowhere does it say “we are taking on the establishment head on”. So if you are expecting that then you will be disappointed. 

If you are looking for a simple, easy to use, forever evolving, versatile, exciting note app then you will love this. You can have multi layer tags - for example Todo and then under that ‘to buy’, ‘to blog’, ‘to pack’ whatever. It syncs across devices instantly. If you create something with a tick list it will show you how far through your ticks you’ve got. Having used all the established names in the past I’ve got to say that this takes the best of all of them and makes it better. Multiple notebooks? Check. Copy off safari? Yup. Headings, fonts, lists? Oh yes. I love it, and I am super proud to be along for the journey of BEAR.

Easy interface to help with keeping focuses on the task of writing. Additionally, the paid features are an extra, rather than compulsory, meaning that you don't have to worry about forking out in order to write a few extra notes.
I use Bear across my phone and 2 iPads. It’s immense! Every day I’m building my own personal wiki which comes with me wherever I go. It’s incredibly powerful.

title.label: Almost perfect app. Still need a web version

content.label:
This is the perfect 4 star app until a web version or Dropbox/Google Drive/One Drive integration is developed 
Using tags for notes is the perfect way to get organised! And the ability to link notes and have multiple tags per note will help you be very productive.

Wanted an alternative to Day One for work use! This app is almost perfect! It looks and feels great! I just wish I could organize notes by the date of my choice and to be able to change the date stamp. A calendar view in the app would be fabulous too!!

I've switched several times between Onenote and Evernote. I've tried various other alternatives, never able to commit to a single app. Until now!

I don't like the concept of adding more and more features to try and do everything well. Somehow people feel that this attracts a wider audience. 

Invariably, it ends with a rich feature set where nothing is absolutely right. Bear focuses on doing a few things really really well. And it does them better than its competitors.

If you want an effective, uncluttered, attractive, responsive application then look no further. I certainly won't be :)

I liked the idea of bear’s minimal design but it has become quite bloated. Eg I typed a word which coincidentally autocompleted to one of bear’s fancy location things. There’s no way to delete this association. Furthermore, when I emailed to report this I was told that it wouldn’t be fixed. This then meant bear was unusable for me. Poor design thinking and the usual “Hey! Let’s add lots of features!” attitude. Very shortsighted. A waste of my money

title.label: Great handy product with delicate design

content.label:
Bravo to the typography design and the Bear team. I’ve been enjoying the logo in App Store for a while, finally decided to give a go when I saw my colleague is using Bear.

But I don’t like subscription. :(

—The end—

I thought it looked pretty cool but when I saw the emojis I cringed so much omg please ditch the emojis. The app has a nice minimalistic theme but the addition of emojis in the introduction made it kind of cringey  ~ sorry
Having searched a lot, this one is hands down the best. And it deserves the premium, mostly out for respect, but for the sync feature as well. And the themes (amazing). Fully recommend it.

Very rarely write reviews, but this app is astounding. One of those apps that has features you didn’t know you needed until you have them.  SO intuitive - one of the most useful apps for writers. Automatically grouping notes based on a hashtag is just lovely. Looks so good too. Brilliant!

this app is so lovely - the interface is beautiful and very easy and smooth to use. one thing i would improve about the app though is for there to be a button that lets you go to the bottom of a note rather than having to scroll all the way through if it’s particularly long. :)

title.label: Great app so far but can be better

content.label:
Great app, good experience so far but a couple of small features would make it even nicer.
 I would really like to see some touch id lock feature for your notes and some sort of reminder feature to catch up with something you started last night and have to finish today or something like that. These is the only reason i am giving 3stars....oh one more thing, it would be really great if the red bear background from the loading screen would switch to the same colour of the theme and icon when they are changed.
Works great and syncs fairly quickly. The ability to scan a documents within the app will be fantastic. Photos are ok scanning would be better.

title.label: Clean and a feeling of space with no clutter

content.label:
Brilliant App. Clean, a feeling of space without clutter. Very happy to pay a subscription.  Good development needs to be supported if we wish to have Apps which are fit for purpose.  I don't understand those who merely  vote the app down because of a small fee.  Bear is simple and uncomplicated to use and I am very happy to have found such a nice piece of development. 

Update: November 2017

Used Bear for nearly a year now. Very happy with the App and the support. Regular updates that work!  I use this App every day, and I am looking forward to another 12 months of use. The small fee to support development of this App is the right way to go and there’s no second thoughts here.

title.label: A wonderful and charming notes app

content.label:
Having got bored with other popular note taking apps and finding the native iPhone notes quite limiting, I downloaded this when seeing it recommended on the editors choice list. It really is a beautiful little app the let’s you simply craft notes, yet adds enough flexibility and freedom to create almost anything. 

I especially like the numerous touches if you read the getting started notes that come pre installed. Charming illustrations of bears which always make you feel happy yet remaining a serious and powerful writing tool. Love it!!

title.label: The Notes app that Apple should have made

content.label: Amazing app. Dropping Apple Notes and my Evernote subscription to use only Bear for my thesis work.
